properties.name: ROOT CAUSE (walked, measured): a chat looking for "link an actor to a capability" searched find_tools six times and found the relation only through describe_schema. INTERACTS_WITH (Actor to anything) exists, but find_tools ranks tools only, the relation has no typed tool, and find_tools' reply never points to describe_schema's from/to
properties.statement:
RUN AS THE SKILL (root-cause), 2026-10-25, on Anthony's ask from the flo2 usage baseline (hub fact:flo2-usage-baseline-2026-10-25).
① OBSERVED from flo2.io's call log (connector_calls, read-only, edge and node types only): on 2026-10-10 between 14:35:03 and 14:35:34, Alex's Grok chat called find_tools six times ("link actor to capability performed by operated by uses", "actor uses capability interacts performs", "interacts_with actor capability uses", "edge from actor to node involves participates_in" and two more). At 14:35:40 it called describe_schema, and at 14:35:57 and 14:35:58 it drew two INTERACTS_WITH edges with create_edge, both ok.
② PRECEDENT: fact:find-tools-misses-split-into-a-vocabulary-gap-no-ranking-can-close-and-a-scorer-that-lets-long-descriptions-crowd (2026-09-11), measured on a corpus of TOOL queries only; req:every-served-tool-is-reachable-by-find-tools-on-a-users-words (proposed); req:vocabulary-covers-personnel ("who performs a function", deferred).
③-⑤ CANDIDATES, each with the measurement that could refute it:
(C1) the schema has no Actor-to-Capability relation. REFUTED: describe_schema from Actor to Capability lists INTERACTS_WITH, declared from Actor to any type, and Alex's chat drew it.
(C2) find_tools searches tools only, and a relation with no typed helper is invisible to it. Refuted if find_tools surfaces INTERACTS_WITH. MEASURED on 0.91.0: even the query "INTERACTS_WITH edge from an actor" ranks add_actor, delete_edge and create_edge, and names no relation. The tool list holds no interacts_with tool. find_tools' description says it ranks "the served surface itself (name, description, parameter names ...)". SURVIVES.
(C3, outside reflow2) the Grok chat searched badly. Its queries name the job plainly ("link actor to capability"), so this is not established as a cause. What is measured: find_tools' reply says to call describe_schema with `tool` once a tool's name is known. It never says that "what joins an X to a Y?" is describe_schema with from and to, which is the call that found it. SURVIVES as a contributor: the pointer is missing.
(C4) the observation is wrong: nothing failed. PARTLY TRUE: the chat recorded the right relation. The cost was six extra calls and about 37 seconds, not a lost capture. My first reading in the baseline ("fell back to a generic edge") was wrong: create_edge carried the right relation.
⑥ CLASS: reflow2's vocabulary has two halves, the typed tools and the schema's node and edge types. find_tools reaches only the first, and describe_schema reaches the second only for someone who already knows the type names. Any relation or node type with no typed tool cannot be found by describing the job. The 2026-09-11 corpus could not have caught this, since it held tool queries only. Fix options are with Anthony, none chosen. Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_018ibUbMKCS1yK5W17cncp9P
